verdicts.evidence: lines 185, 187-200, 202-215, 218-237: Try again reloads, Save team name calls renameTeam, Send invite calls inviteMember and re-renders, Remove calls removeMember, 'Invite X back' re-invites. No button lacks a handler.

line 6: <title> hardcodes 'Team settings - Northwind Studio'; the team name in the tab never comes from api.getTeam and stays wrong after a rename (193) or a failed load. All in-page values (164-171) do come from the api.
lines 42-84: one screen of independent sections; no step depends on an earlier screen. The undo bar (227) names the removed person in place.
lines 45-50, 68-76: each task has one or two single-line inputs, one step, no long free text.
line 74: invite role preselects Member, the lower-privilege value. Checkboxes take server values (169). Enter submits only rename or invite (187, 202), never removal.
lines 43-83: a settings screen with six occasional tasks and no single dominant frequent one; all are done inline anyway.

lines 43-83: four sections (team name, members with role select and remove, invite, email notifications) each match a brief task. No stat cards or extras; Last active column (59) is a member field in the same table.
line 49: only 'Save team name' has class primary. Send invite (75), Try again (39), Remove (159) and the undo button (227) use the plain style.
line 159: Remove is a plain outlined button in its own Actions column, not primary, outside any form so Enter in a field cannot trigger it.

lines 155, 159: owner row shows text 'Owner' instead of a select and 'The owner cannot be removed' instead of a button. Selects and checkboxes are disabled only during their own request (243-246, 250-253).
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in lines 34-85 or the render code 150-172.
lines 35-83, 127-141: visible text is headings, labels, task messages. Nothing mentions implementation, the brief, mock data or unfinished features.

line 73: 'Admins can invite and remove people.' sits at the role choice it informs. Line 81: 'Each change is saved as you make it.' sits on the checkboxes it governs. Line 159: owner reason in place of the control. No banners.
lines 73, 81: remaining guidance is one short line at the control concerned. Line 63 'Invite the first member below.' is the empty-state next step, one line. No 'This page lets you' style narration.

lines 73, 81: helper and legend text add new facts, not restatements. Note lines 44 and 46 repeat 'Team name' as heading and label verbatim, but a label is not a subtitle, description, helper or tooltip under the test.
lines 35-83, 136-141, 195, 212, 227: plain factual text, no greeting, slogan, exclamation mark or congratulation.
lines 39, 49, 75, 159, 227: 'Try again', 'Save team name', 'Send invite', 'Remove <name>', 'Invite <name> back'. Each starts with a specific verb and names its object where several are in view.
lines 127-128, 133: roles mapped to Owner/Admin/Member, notification keys mapped to plain labels, null lastActive shown as 'Not yet signed in', dates formatted. No ids, enum values or codes shown.

lines 38, 136-141, 234, 245, 252: messages name the problem and next step ('The connection dropped, so this was not saved. Try again.', 'All 12 seats are in use. Remove someone or add seats...'). Raw ECONNRESET text is never shown.
lines 20, 38, 137-140, 234, 245, 252: neutral wording with a 'Problem:' prefix; no 'invalid', 'failed', 'oops', exclamation marks or capitals. Subject is the problem.
lines 63, 151: with zero members the text 'No one is on this team yet. Invite the first member below.' shows, and the invite form (66-77) is the next step on the same screen.
lines 37-40, 182 vs 63, 151: failed load shows a bordered panel 'Team settings could not be loaded...' with Try again; empty team shows 'No one is on this team yet' with invite. No filters exist.

lines 181-183: load failure shows message and retry. 196-198, 213: rename and invite failures show inline text and keep the typed value. 245, 252: role and checkbox revert with a named message. 234: remove failure stated, row kept.

line 176: 'Loading team settings...' set before the await. 143-148: buttons switch to Saving.../Sending invite.../Removing... at once. 243, 250: selects and checkboxes disable and status says Saving. Calls cap at 1.5s.
lines 175-180: #content (which holds the empty message and table) is hidden until getTeam resolves and render() has run; only the loading text shows during the wait.

lines 23-26: table in an overflow-x wrapper, cells use overflow-wrap:anywhere, row actions wrap. Line 133: null lastActive becomes 'Not yet signed in'. Line 16: inputs max-width 100%. No undefined or null can print.
lines 258-260: beforeunload prompts when the team name field differs from the saved name. Roles and notifications save immediately (239-255).
lines 69-70: the only format-bound field is labelled 'Email address' with type=email, which states the expected format before typing. Team name has no format rule beyond non-empty.
lines 45-50, 68-76: rename has one required field; invite has a required email and a role select with a default. No optional fields exist.

lines 187-190, 202-206: validation runs only in submit handlers; there are no input or keyup listeners. A corrected resubmit replaces the error with the status text and removes aria-invalid (194-195, 211-212).
lines 47-48, 70-71: rename-msg and invite-msg sit directly under their inputs. Line 20: errors carry a 'Problem:' text prefix as well as red colour.
lines 190, 196-198: rename never clears the input on rejection. Lines 205-213: invite clears the email only on success (211); on failure the typed email stays.
lines 190, 205: a rejected submit sets aria-invalid and focuses the field. Lines 47, 70: inputs reference their message with aria-describedby; messages are role=alert (48, 71).
lines 49, 75: submit buttons are never disabled. Lines 190, 206: submitting empty or malformed input shows 'Enter a team name.' or 'Enter a full email address...' and focuses the field.

lines 143-148: busy() returns early when the button already has aria-busy=true, changes the label to Saving.../Sending invite... and dims it (14) until the response. Enter in the field goes through the same guard.
lines 146, 176, 243, 250: every click or change synchronously changes a button label, disables the control or writes status text before the awaited call.

lines 195, 210-212, 225-227, 244, 251: 'Team name saved.', new row plus 'Invite sent to ...', row removed plus undo bar, '<name> is now admin.', 'Saved.'. Every catch branch writes a failure message (197, 213, 234, 245, 252).

lines 195, 212, 244, 251: messages report server confirmation that the unchanged input, select or checkbox would not otherwise show, and that an invite email went out. The removal message (227) carries the undo action.
No setTimeout outside the simulated server. Errors are written into in-place regions (38, 48, 55, 71, 82) and the undo bar (227) stays until used or replaced; nothing auto-dismisses.
lines 217-232: Remove runs at once with no confirmation, then shows '<name> was removed and has lost access.' with an 'Invite <name> back' button that re-invites with the same email and role.
Brief says a removed person can be invited again, and the page treats removal as reversible with undo (217-232). Rename and role changes can be changed back. No permanent delete or payment.
No confirm() calls and no dialog element in the markup (34-85); the only prompt is the browser's unsaved-changes guard (258-260).

lines 245, 252: when changeRole or setNotification fails, the select is set back to the previous role and the checkbox is flipped back, with '... was not changed. The connection dropped, so this was not saved. Try again.'
No dialog element is created or opened; the dialog CSS rule on line 30 is unused.
No modal dialog is opened anywhere in lines 126-262.

lines 35-83: the heading is followed directly by the working sections in the brief's order (name, members, invite, notifications), all of equal weight; no decorative or secondary block sits above them.
lines 35-44: h1 'Team settings', then the first form. No hero, greeting or intro panel.
No stat cards, summary numbers or charts in lines 34-85; the seat count appears only inside an error sentence (138).
The members table (57-62) has no filter, search, sort or column controls.

All controls are native button, input, select and checkbox elements (39-81, 155-159, 169). Focus is managed after actions: retry (182), invalid field (190, 205), undo button (232), re-enabled control (246, 253).
line 20: red error text also gets a 'Problem:' prefix. Lines 146, 14: busy state is a label change as well as opacity. Roles and status are text (155-157, 195).

lines 36, 48, 55, 71, 82: role=status and role=alert regions exist in the page before any message is written to them (131, 195, 212, 234, 245, 252). Note success text for rename and invite lands in role=alert regions.
No accordions, custom menus, comboboxes or tabs; only native select elements (74, 155).

lines 5, 9, 16, 23-27: viewport meta, fluid main with 16px padding, inputs capped at 100%, table in a horizontal scroll wrapper with wrapping cells and wrapping row actions, no fixed widths and no dialogs, so each task stays reachable at 375px.
